_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: near_eastern (akkadian) backbone + old_persian (axsatran) substrate (intra-family blend, Akkadian-leaning)

blend.backbone: near_eastern (akkadian: the alu/bit river-cities of the Two Rivers, the sangu temple-priesthood, construct-chain toponyms, emphatic gutturals q/kh/sh/', mimation -u/-um/-tu, SOV agglutinative grammar, penultimate stress)
blend.substrate: old_persian (axsatran: the highland uplands and the satrapal court, the flowing -a/-ah/-iya vowels and the ezafe genitive-of-relation, the horse-and-road material register, the paridaida garden and the apadana hall)
blend.lean: Akkadian-heavy - a Perso-Akkadian crown over the Two Rivers' temple-cities: Babylon and Persepolis made one. The Akkadian scribal-priestly city is the spine - its rule, kin, temple and land register endure - while the Persian highland court lends the throne-word (the Shah), the courtly and material vocabulary, and the garden-and-cavalry flavor of the upland aristocracy.

_note: NEW intra-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_03 Shinarur (Mesopotamian/Akkadian) x BASE_04 (Persian/Axsatran). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Mesopotamian base = Civilized and Persian base = Civilized, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Parsur is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Mesopotamian (Akkadian) realm fused with Persia - the Two Rivers' temple-cities under a Perso-Akkadian crown, Babylon and Persepolis as one. Backbone/lean = Akkadian (the alu-cities, the bit-ili temples, the scribal populace, the rule/kin/temple register, the construct-chain toponyms); substrate = Old Persian (the highland satrapal court, the courtly/material/staple words, the flowing vowels and ezafe endings). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Akkadian register (allowed, catalog 5.3); the kingdom-tier display ruler is the approved foreign term 'Shah' (the Persian throne, recorded in approved_foreign_terms_used). DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Akkadian Sargonid reflexes PRIMARY, Old-Persian variants SECONDARY), never real Mesopotamian/Iranian gods. All three alignments (standard lens). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English (or the approved 'Shah'); conlang titles live in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. The lexicon is a SINGLE FUSED TONGUE (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md), not slash-pairs.

phonology.palette: Akkadian backbone - emphatic and guttural consonants (q, kh, h, ', sh, ts), triconsonantal roots, a/i/u vowels, -u/-um/-tu endings, mimation, construct chains, penultimate stress - meeting an Old Persian substrate: flowing vowels (long a/i/u, the -a/-ah/-iya/-ana endings), the spirants th/x/f, the ezafe genitive-of-relation, the horse-element -aspa and the glory-element -farnah. Per the CSV: emphatic consonants with flowing vowels; grammar SOV with a root-based ezafe construction (the Persian relational chain absorbed into the Akkadian construct-state). Theophoric on the Akkadian reflexes (Tullaru-, Urlandu-, Numunu-) with Old-Persian construct variants (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC backbone with Akkadian mimation -um and construct chains; Persian clusters (sp-, st-, fr-, thr-) admitted and softened toward the Akkadian inventory; flowing Persian -a/-ah/-iya endings adapted onto Akkadian -u/-um stems; penultimate stress throughout; construct toponyms Bit-/Dur-/Kar- woven with the ezafe relation.

sound_changes: Old Persian flowing endings adapt to Akkadian inflection: final -a/-ah/-iya/-ana > -u/-um/-tu (rautah > rautu, kaufa > kaufu, vana > banu); roots take Akkadian case-vowels and mimation
Persian spirants/clusters collapse into the Akkadian emphatic inventory: th > t/ts, x(kh) retained as kh, f > p, z retained, sp-/st-/fr-/thr- simplified or fronted (spaita > pisaitu, fra- > pir-)
Akkadian penultimate stress imposed on all words; the Persian ezafe '-ahya' relation is absorbed into the Akkadian construct state (X-of-Y = Y-construct + X)
retain Akkadian sh, ', q and the construct chain; retain a few Persian signatures - the -aspa (horse), -farnah (glory) and Arta- (truth) elements survive as audible loan-morphs on Akkadianized stems
very short or vowel-final roots take an Akkadian -u/-um/-tu ending so the whole tongue rhymes Akkadian
fusion_rules.source_tilt: courtly/highland/material/staple words from Old Persian roots (the upland court and its goods: aspa-horse, zaranya-gold, paridaida-garden, kaufa-mountain, yava-grain); rule/kin/temple/land words from Akkadian roots (the scribal-priestly spine: sharru-king, mar-son, bit-ili-temple, naru-river, ugaru-plain); every root then filtered to one Akkadian-shaped phonology
portmanteaus: city alu+pura>alpuru (the temple-city wedded to the Persian -pura)
fort dimtu+dida>dimdidu (the river-fort and the Persian stronghold)
temple bit-ili+atashana>bitashanu (the god-house and the fire-temple as one)
garden kiru+paridaida>kirdaidu (the walled paradise-grove over the Akkadian orchard)
horse-lord redu+asabara>redasparu (the Akkadian soldier and the Persian cavalier fused)
sacred ellu+yazata>elyaztu (the holy made one word)

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Akkadian rule/kin/temple/land roots + Old-Persian courtly/highland/material/staple roots, all run through one Akkadian-shaped sound-law (flowing Persian endings -> -u/-um/-tu, penultimate stress, construct/ezafe chains); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. NO slash-pairs - this is one tongue.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Akkadian scribal-priestly populace keep the 'mar-' (son of) patronymic and theophoric constructs; the Persian-descended upland court keep a house (vith-, Akkadianized to vit-) and a satrapal/court office; the throne fuses both - a Sharru who also carries a Bit- house-name and the Persian farnah-glory. Order given-first.
morphology.compounding_rule: Akkadian construct-chains (Bit-[god], Dur-[ruler], Kar-[god]) absorbing the Persian ezafe genitive-of-relation: the capital Parsur (Parsa + the Two Rivers' -ur), Dur-Sharru (king's-fort), Atash-Tullaru (fire of Tullaru) on the Akkadian construct frame; resource + feature (Zaranu-kaufu, the gold-mountain).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Perso-Akkadian crown over the Two Rivers' temple-cities: the Shah and his rubu-kin at the throne, the shaknu-governors over the alu-cities, the hazannu-mayors and the turtanu-commanders beneath; the Persian-descended marz-wardens hold the highland marches; the sangu-priesthood and the scribal ekallu serve the crown as they have served every crown)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Akkadian native ladder, ascending, beneath an English display ladder (Baron/Marquis/Count/Duke/Prince/[Shah]/Emperor). The kingdom-tier DISPLAY ruler is the approved foreign term 'Shah' (the Persian throne-word, the one Persian title the realm wears openly); all other display tiers are English. Native: Hazannu (mayor) barony; Massaru (warden) march; Shaknu (appointed governor) county; Turtanu (commander-in-chief) duchy; Rubu (prince) principality; Sharru (king; styled the Shah) kingdom over a Sharrutu; Shar-kishshati (king of the totality) empire over the Kishshatu. The highland Persian-descended marz-wardens and the satrapal usage survive in regional flavor beneath the Akkadian frame. The sangu (priest) and the scribal shatammu stand outside the ladder. Rank titles are the real Akkadian register (allowed); 'Shah' is the approved foreign display term.
title_ladder.heir: Mar-Sharri (son of the king / crown prince; the Shah's heir)

honorifics.champion: Redasparu (the horse-lord; Akkadian redu + Persian asabara)

vassalage.vassal: Ardu (servant) / Bandaku (the king's bondsman; Persian bandaka, Akkadianized)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler' - here 'Shah' at the kingdom tier). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Akkadian city-stock carry a theophoric given name + mar- patronymic; the Persian-descended upland court carry a virtue/theophoric given + a vit- house and a court office; order given-first.
surname_source: Bit- / Vit- house (Akkadian construct / Persian vith)
office (shaknu, turtanu, marz-warden) or honest-deed byname
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Akkadian scribal city-folk keep theophoric names (X-iddina, Warad-X) on the morphed canon-stems; the Persian-descended court keep virtue-and-theophoric names (Arta-X truth-names, X-farnah glory-names) on the shifted stems; the throne fuses both.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Akkadian devotional constructs: Warad-Tullaru (servant of Tullaru), Tullaru-iddina (Tullaru-gave-me); Persian-flavored variants on the shifted stems: Baga-Turvasa (god-Turvasa), Arta-shum (truth-name), X-farnah (glory-of-X). e.g. Tullaru-iddina, Turvasa-data, Artafarnu.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Akkadian Sargonid reflexes PRIMARY (the family_near_eastern / hammuran morphs), Old-Persian variants SECONDARY (the axsatran shifted stems), never real Mesopotamian/Iranian gods. All three alignments (standard lens). The Akkadian temple-cult is the spine; the Persian fire-and-Arta register is the courtly overlay - the crown keeps both the bit-ili god-house and the atash fire-altar.
religion.the_one: Itarnu (Akkadian; Persian Asturna) - the great distant one, honored not petitioned, source of the Shah's farnah-glory

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tullaru (Persian Turvasa) - the sun and judgment, lamp of right-order
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Urlandu (Persian Urlaspa) - iron, oath, war and the cavalier
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gayandu (Persian Gayanta) - the enduring earth and mountain
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Numunu (Persian Naumana) - sky, the good mind and scribe-wisdom
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Rialtu (Persian Riyata) - the mother, the Lady of Waters, mercy
sample_deity_renames.Argentus: Argantu (Persian Arzanta) - trade, the road and increase

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Itarnu the distant, Tullaru the just, Urlandu of the sworn war, Rialtu the merciful, Numunu of the law-stele - upholding the right-order (the Persian Arta) and naming the Chaotic powers -lemnu (evil) or the hosts of the Lie, warded; the law-stele and the fire-altar bind alike
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral dead (kept as fravartu, the honored fore-spirits, after the Persian fravashi) and the city-spirits of the bit-ili; the great powers invoked at the temple and the atash fire-altar situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, the hosts of the Lie, and names the Lawful powers - and Itarnu - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as -lemnu (Akkadian evil) or the hosts of Drauga (the Persian Lie), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marakshu the City-Burner (Persian Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities); Vacidus -> Bakidu-lemnu the Unmaking (Persian Vakida the Devouring-Void); Lusanto -> Lusanu the Hoard-Worm (Persian Lusanta the Coin-Serpent).
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Bit-ili (god-house/temple) of [power] and its Atash (fire of [power]): 'the Bit-ili of Tullaru', 'the Atash of Tullaru'.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified law-givers and just kings of the cities, kept as fravartu (fore-spirits) and inscribed on the temple-stele; honored at the ziggurat and the fire-altar; 'the Just [name]', 'the Arta-true [name]'.

holy_symbol_motifs.Tullaru: a winged sun-disc over a law-stele and a fire-altar
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlandu: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring
holy_symbol_motifs.Gayandu: the alluvial field beneath the ziggurat and the mountain
